picks.title: Canva's first AI image model plans designs before generating them
picks.excerpt: Canva released Craft, its first in-house image generation model, built for design layouts rather than photography: it plans a composition before generating it, putting Canva in direct competition with OpenAI, Google and Microsoft image models.
picks.rationale: A major new model release from a core design platform. Craft is Canva's first in-house image model, built to plan layouts rather than make photos. Nothing about Canva appears in the 30-day history.

picks.title: How Lufthansa Systems prototypes realistic maps for the cockpit with Figma Make
picks.excerpt: Lufthansa Systems' designers use Figma Make's AI prompt-to-prototype flow to build dynamic, data-realistic cockpit map prototypes for pilot user testing instead of static mockups.
picks.rationale: A named enterprise case: Lufthansa Systems swapped static mockups for data-realistic Figma Make prototypes in pilot testing. Designers can copy the workflow directly. It is distinct from the earlier Figma agent, Specs and code-layers posts.

picks.title: I gave my coding agent a color palette library, and stopped pasting hex codes
picks.excerpt: A developer wires a structured color palette library into Claude as a tool so the coding agent pulls accessible, named design colors instead of inventing six random hex codes.
picks.rationale: A practical setup you can try tomorrow: give a coding agent a structured color library as a tool so it stops inventing hex codes. This is a different technique from the 10-22 de-slop skill and the 10-08 design-system test.

picks.title: Lock In Character Likeness for AI Posters in Firefly
picks.excerpt: Adobe tutorial: use a reference-sheet trick in Firefly so an AI-generated subject stays recognizable across every pose, angle and scene of a poster series.
picks.rationale: An official Adobe how-to that solves a common problem: keeping a character consistent across a whole Firefly poster series. No Firefly character-consistency item appears in the history.

picks.title: AI's next bottleneck is the engineer's desk
picks.excerpt: Nomic is helping Arcadis automate engineering design reviews with AI, but the article argues the next bottleneck is human checking of AI-generated design output.
picks.rationale: A named deployment: Nomic is automating Arcadis's engineering design reviews. It brings an AEC and CAD angle to the brief. Its history_match, the 10-21 UX Collective attention essay, only shares the word 'bottleneck'; they are different stories.
